title: Amazon opens its first delivery station in Puerto Rico, bringing faster shipping and new jobs
summary: The Dorado site cuts San Juan–area delivery times from up to two weeks to about two days and adds more than 100 jobs and about 300 driver roles.
body_markdown:
---


## Key takeaways


- Amazon’s new delivery station in Dorado is the company’s first operations site in Puerto Rico and the Caribbean.


- El Area Metro area customers can now get packages in about two days, down from up to two weeks.


- The station employs more than 100 people and supports about 300 new delivery driver roles.


---


Amazon has officially opened its first delivery station in Puerto Rico. The 100,000-square-foot site in Dorado is the company’s first operations facility on the island, and it serves customers across the San Juan metro area.


For those customers, orders that once took as long as two weeks can now arrive in about two days. The station started making deliveries in August, ahead of its official opening on November 16.


Amazon's first delivery station in Puerto Rico, located in Dorado, is now open, bringing two-day delivery to customers across the San Juan metro area.


The station is also bringing more than 100 jobs and about 300 driver roles to Puerto Rico, part of Amazon’s ongoing investment to expand its delivery network and create opportunities across the island. Hiring is underway ahead of the holiday season.


## How the Dorado delivery station speeds up shipping in Puerto Rico


Delivery stations are the last stop before a package reaches a customer. Packages come in, get sorted by route, and are loaded into vans for the final leg of the trip.


With a station in Dorado, packages for customers in the El Area Metro area can now be sorted and sent out locally. That’s what brings delivery times down to about two days.


[Amazon invests another $1.9 billion in the Delivery Service Partner program, launching new safety initiatives and AI-powered technology](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/transportation/amazon-dsp-program-investment-2026)


Amazon has invested $21.7 billion to support DSPs and their Delivery Associates throughout the eight-year program history.


Puerto Rico Governor Jenniffer González-Colón, Dorado Mayor Aníbal José Torres, and other local leaders joined Amazon to mark the station’s opening.


“Amazon’s arrival and continued expansion in Puerto Rico demonstrate the confidence that major companies have in our island and the talent of our people,” said Governor González-Colón. “This 100,000-square-foot delivery station in Dorado creates job opportunities, strengthens our logistics infrastructure, and helps accelerate the delivery of thousands of packages daily to Puerto Rican consumers. Our administration remains committed to fostering a business-friendly environment that encourages investment, innovation, and economic development. We also recognize Amazon’s commitment. We will continue working to attract investments that create jobs, strengthen our economy, and generate new opportunities for all Puerto Ricans.”


Amazon's new delivery station in Puerto Rico is creating more than 100 jobs and approximately 300 driver roles on the island.


“When we broke ground in Dorado, we promised Puerto Rico faster, better service, and today we’re delivering on that,” said Ashleigh de la Torre, vice president of public policy at Amazon. “We’re grateful to Governor González-Colón, Mayor Torres, and local leaders for their partnership, and we’re excited for everything still ahead as we continue to grow here.”


## How the Dorado station is bringing new jobs to Puerto Rico


The Dorado station employs more than 100 people. Six


[Delivery Service Partners](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/policy-news-views/amazon-dsp-program-update) (DSPs), which are independent businesses that deliver Amazon packages, also operate out of the site. Together they support about 300 new driver roles.


Amazon's Dorado delivery station serves as the final stop before packages reach customers across the El Área Metro region.


“For Dorado, it is a source of great pride and gratitude that Amazon chose our city for its first distribution center in Puerto Rico,” said Mayor Torres. “This investment marks an important step in the economic development of our municipality and the entire island. It strengthens our ability to attract new opportunities, supports commercial activity, and creates pathways for our people to take part in a project with global reach.”


## How Amazon is supporting nonprofits in Puerto Rico


As part of the facility’s opening, Amazon has donated $40,000 to Virtus Puerto Rico. The local nonprofit helps athletes with intellectual impairments, autism, and related conditions get access to coaching and athletic development, along with adaptive workforce and career opportunities.


The donation builds on Amazon’s support for the island. Since 2022, the company has contributed more than $100,000 directly to Puerto Rico nonprofits, including Virtus Puerto Rico, Fundación Rimas, and Sauce for Cause.
